children: Palm oil prices ended lower, pressured by concerns over elevated Malaysian inventories and expectations for strong October production, while uncertainties surrounding export demand continue to weigh on market sentiment, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. Ng expects CPO futures to find support around 4,650 ringgit a ton and face resistance at 4,850 ringgit a ton, with traders closely monitoring soybean oil and crude oil prices for further direction, he adds. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for January delivery ended 25 ringgit lower at 4,793 ringgit a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
